# About Berg Advisors

## Identity
Berg Advisors is a CPA firm founded more than 30 years ago, originally based in Newtown Square, Pennsylvania (18 Campus Blvd, Suite 100, Room 103), and now operating as a fully virtual firm serving clients across the country and around the world with no geographic concentration. The firm is led by Managing Partner Andrew C. Berg, CPA, who has practiced as a CPA for over 30 years and built the firm around being a strategic advisor and proactive partner rather than a once-a-year service provider. Berg Advisors is a member of AICPA, PASBA, and PICPA, and is affiliated with Woodard, Canopy, and Profit First Professionals. The team includes Partners Megan M. Murray and Joshua Beaugrand, CPA; Director of Client Services Lindsey Coburn, CPA; Director of Outsourced Accounting Veil Velarde, CPA; Director of Compliance/Tax Michael Laudazio; Senior Accountant Julia Lindner, EA; and Senior Accountant Karl Louie Hipolito. Berg Advisors has been recognized as a Woodard Top 50 Client Accounting Services Award Firm (2023 Spotlight), an Intuit Firm of the Future, and a Canopy 2021 Innovation Award Finalist. Andrew Berg has spoken at AICPA conferences and appeared as a guest on the Profit First Professionals podcast.

## Positioning & Differentiation
Berg Advisors positions itself as the CPA firm that treats clients' businesses like family — combining proactive communication, flat monthly fees, and more than 30 years of expertise across e-commerce, property management, and family offices. The firm's brand voice is relationship-driven, proactive, approachable, reassuring, technology-forward, and expert, favoring plain-English explanations over jargon.

Clients typically come to Berg Advisors because they need a firm they can actually talk to and ask questions of, because their small business has outgrown a previous accounting firm, or because they are seeking next-level advice for business strategy rather than year-end compliance alone. Key differentiators include:

- Over 30 years of CPA experience under Managing Partner Andrew C. Berg
- One of the few full-service U.S. firms specializing in e-commerce accrual accounting, inventory accounting, and multi-state sales tax economic nexus
- Fixed, all-inclusive flat monthly fees instead of hourly billing
- Relationship-driven, proactive communication with a mutual success plan for every client
- Woodard Top 50 Accounting Firm and Intuit Firm of the Future recognition

Competitors in the e-commerce accounting space — including SellerCPA, Acuity, Acenteus CCA, AMZ Accountant, and Ledger Labs — focus primarily on bookkeeping and tax for Amazon and Shopify sellers. Berg Advisors differentiates by pairing that same e-commerce specialization (FBA inventory, A2X, marketplace facilitator rules, accrual conversion) with broader advisory work across property management and family office clients, and by emphasizing an ongoing advisory relationship over transactional service.

## Industries Served

### Multi-channel E-commerce
Berg Advisors serves Amazon, Shopify, eBay, Etsy, and Walmart sellers who need accounting, bookkeeping, inventory, and sales tax compliance support. Value proposition: managing financial data from multiple sales channels to ensure accuracy and provide insights for growth, with specialization in accrual accounting, inventory, and complex sales tax nexus. Pain points addressed include reconciling revenue and payouts across platforms with no unified view; understanding true profitability after fees, refunds, and COGS; multi-state sales tax nexus exposure and falling behind on filings; cash-basis books that don't reflect real inventory value or satisfy lenders/investors; FBA inventory accounting including stranded inventory and reimbursements; year-end tax surprises from a lack of proactive planning; confusion over marketplace facilitator laws; and scaling from a single channel to multiple channels without clean financials.

### Family Offices
Berg Advisors supports family-owned businesses and wealth structures that need tailored accounting and cash flow strategy. Value proposition: access to experienced financial professionals who free up time, improve accuracy in record-keeping, and provide peace of mind — helping clients manage their money, know their numbers, and know when they can retire. Pain points addressed include lack of consolidated visibility across multiple entities, accounts, and investments; commingling of personal and business finances; absence of a clear cash flow strategy across generations or business units; difficulty structuring ownership and distributions tax-efficiently; succession planning gaps; reliance on generalist CPAs unfamiliar with complex family wealth structures; avoidable year-end tax bills; and time-consuming financial administration that pulls owners away from running the business.

### Property Management Companies
Berg Advisors works with owner-operators and principals managing residential or commercial rental portfolios. Value proposition: a centralized view of income, expenses, and performance across every property and entity; accurate, on-time owner distributions with a clear paper trail; security deposit and trust accounting handled in full compliance with state regulations; year-end 1099 preparation for vendors and contractors; cash flow reporting by property; end-to-end multi-state filing management; clean separation of business and personal finances; and back-office systems built to scale with the portfolio. Pain points addressed include tracking income and expenses across multiple properties and entities with no centralized view; managing owner distributions; security deposit and trust accounting compliance; time-consuming and error-prone 1099 filing; limited cash flow visibility across a growing portfolio; multi-state filing complexity; mixed personal and business finances; and scaling the portfolio without matching back-office systems.

## A CPA firm that treats your business like family

Founded more than 30 years ago in Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, Berg Advisors started as a local CPA firm and grew into a virtual practice serving e-commerce sellers, family offices, and property management companies nationwide. We kept the part that mattered: knowing our clients by name, not by ticket number.

Most local accounting firms treat you like a transaction, an annual filing, a once-a-year phone call in March. We built something different. Every client gets a written mutual success plan outlining what we're tracking together and how often we'll talk about it. That's the difference between a firm that files your return and one that actually knows your business.

If you searched for a CPA in Chester County and found a firm that still answers the phone like a hometown practice, you found the right one. We just happen to serve clients from Newtown Square to Nevada.

## Over 30 years of experience behind every recommendation

Andrew Berg, CPA, founded the firm on the belief that good advice comes from pattern recognition, seeing what works and what doesn't across hundreds of businesses over three decades. That experience shows up in the details: the sales tax nexus question you didn't know to ask, the accrual conversion your bank will require before your next loan, the entity structure that saves real money at tax time.

The firm's approach has earned outside recognition too. Berg Advisors was named a Woodard Top 50 Client Accounting Services firm in 2023 and was a finalist for Canopy's Innovation Award in 2021. A CPA credential means someone passed an exam. Three decades of client relationships means someone knows what actually happens when a Shopify seller expands into a fourth state, or when a family office needs to untangle personal and business accounts. That's the kind of experience behind every recommendation we make.

## Deep specialization in the industries we know best

Generalist CPAs can handle a basic tax return for almost any business. But multi-channel e-commerce, family offices, and property management each carry accounting problems a once-a-year preparer will miss, inventory accrual, multi-state sales tax nexus, consolidated reporting across a dozen properties or entities. We built our practice around three niches instead of trying to be everything to everyone.

### Multi-Channel E-commerce
icon: Globe

Amazon, Shopify, eBay, Etsy, and Walmart each report revenue differently, and reconciling them by hand creates a mess by Q2. We handle [accrual-basis accounting, inventory costing, and multi-state sales tax nexus](/industries/e-commerce) for product-based sellers, as one of the few full-service U.S. firms built specifically for this.

### Family Offices
icon: Briefcase

Multiple entities, multiple accounts, and investments that don't fit a single ledger. We consolidate the view and keep [personal and business finances properly separated](/industries/family-offices), so nothing gets commingled and nothing gets missed at tax time.

### Property Management Companies
icon: Building2

Tracking income, expenses, and owner distributions across a dozen properties in spreadsheets doesn't scale. We give you [one centralized view of performance by property and by entity](/industries/property-management), built for portfolios that keep growing.

## How we work with you

Most accounting relationships run on two things: hourly invoices and reactive service. Ours doesn't.

- [Flat monthly fees](/pricing-calculator), not surprise invoices. You know exactly what you're paying before the month starts, whether we're deep in a sales tax nexus study or just running payroll.
- Proactive communication. We don't wait for you to call with a problem. Quarterly strategy calls are built into every engagement, and if something in your numbers looks off, we're the ones picking up the phone.
- A mutual success plan. At the start of every engagement, we write down what we're tracking, how often we'll meet, and what working well looks like for your business specifically, not a generic checklist.

This is what year-round tax planning and outsourced accounting are supposed to look like: predictable cost, regular contact, and a plan you actually helped write.

## A team invested in your long-term success

Behind every account at Berg Advisors is a small team of CPAs and EAs, not a rotating cast of junior staff you meet once a year. Joshua Beaugrand, CPA, and Lindsey Coburn, CPA, handle much of the day-to-day tax and accounting work. Veil Velarde, CPA, leads outsourced accounting engagements for growth-stage businesses that need fractional back-office support. Julia Lindner, EA, represents clients directly to the IRS when a notice or audit shows up in the mailbox.

We explain things in plain English, not accountant-speak, because the goal is for you to understand your own numbers, not just receive them. Michael Laudazio handles the multi-entity, multi-state compliance work that keeps growing businesses out of trouble with state tax authorities. It's a small team on purpose: fewer handoffs, fewer people who don't know your name. You can [meet the full team here](/about-us/meet-the-team).

## How our team works with you all year long

Every new client starts with a mutual success plan, a written agreement on what gets delivered, when, and how the team communicates, so nobody's guessing three months in.

### Onboarding and mutual success plan
We map your entities, platforms, and prior-year numbers, then agree on a success plan that spells out deliverables and deadlines both sides sign off on.

### Monthly close and reporting
Bookkeeping and reconciliations close every month, not once a quarter, so you're reviewing last month's numbers instead of last year's.

### Quarterly strategy calls
A CPA gets on the phone with you every quarter to talk through cash flow, tax strategy, and whatever's changed in the business since the last call.

### Flat monthly fee
You're billed the same amount whether this month's questions take ten minutes or two hours. No surprise invoices for picking up the phone.

### Best E-Commerce CPA Services for Online Businesses
URL: /industries/e-commerce

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: ecommerce-multichannel-seller-review.jpg | alt: "Business owner reviewing multi-channel sales reports on a laptop" | query: "small business owner reviewing sales reports" -->
## A CPA firm built for multi-channel selling

Amazon, Shopify, Walmart, eBay, and Etsy sellers don't need a generalist who dabbles in e-commerce between real estate closings and payroll runs. They need a firm that already knows what a settlement report looks like, why FBA reimbursements matter, and how cost of goods sold gets calculated when inventory sits in three different warehouses at once.

Berg Advisors brings more than 30 years of combined CPA experience to the table, with [Andrew C. Berg, CPA,](/about-us/meet-the-team) leading the firm's work with product-based businesses, from single-channel Shopify shops to sellers running Amazon, Walmart, and Etsy storefronts side by side. As a virtual firm working with sellers in all 50 states, geography never limits who gets access to this expertise, though the firm's origins trace back to Newtown Square, Pennsylvania.

Unlike single-channel specialists who only speak Amazon, or local accountants who treat e-commerce as a side practice, this firm runs on a flat monthly fee, not an hourly clock. Asking a question about your margins doesn't cost extra, and a call before tax season isn't a billable event.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: multichannel-revenue-reconciliation.jpg | alt: "Accountant comparing sales data from multiple online marketplaces" | query: "accountant analyzing financial spreadsheets" -->
## Solving the multi-channel reconciliation headache

Every marketplace exports data differently. Amazon settlement reports bury fees inside multi-week batches. Shopify mixes gross sales with discounts and shipping income. Walmart, eBay, and Etsy each format payouts their own way, and reconciling all of it by hand eats a weekend every month.

Berg Advisors builds one unified ledger from every channel you sell on, so gross revenue, marketplace fees, refunds, and shipping costs land where they belong instead of getting lumped into "miscellaneous." Your P&L ends up reflecting what each channel earns, not a blended guess.

Once the numbers reconcile, the real question gets easier to answer: which channel, product, or SKU is making money. That's the conversation this firm has with clients every quarter, not just once a year at tax time.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: inventory-accrual-accounting.jpg | alt: "Warehouse inventory shelves with boxes ready for shipment" | query: "warehouse inventory shelves boxes" -->
## Accrual accounting and inventory done right

Cash-basis books work fine for a lemonade stand. They fall apart the moment a bank, investor, or lender asks for GAAP-compliant financials, or when a seller can't tell if last month was profitable because inventory purchases and revenue landed in different periods.

Andrew C. Berg, CPA, works directly with growing product businesses moving from cash-basis to accrual accounting, the shift banks and investors expect once a company outgrows its founder's personal checking account. That includes proper inventory costing, so landed costs, freight, and per-unit COGS show up correctly instead of getting expensed the day a container clears customs.

Full-service firms that handle this well are hard to find. Most bookkeeping shops stop at cash-basis reconciliation and hand you an incomplete picture right when accurate numbers matter most.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: sales-tax-nexus-map.jpg | alt: "Map highlighting multiple US states for sales tax nexus" | query: "map united states business expansion" -->
## Multi-state sales tax nexus without the guesswork

Selling on Amazon FBA alone can create sales tax nexus in a dozen states before you've shipped a single order there yourself, because inventory sits in fulfillment centers you don't control. Add a warehouse in a new state, cross an economic nexus threshold, or launch on a new marketplace, and the filing requirements shift again.

Andrew C. Berg, CPA, advises product-based businesses on nexus exposure as they expand, turning that mess into a plan instead of a scramble.

- Nexus review across every state you sell into, based on inventory location and revenue thresholds
- Registration and filing setup handled ahead of time, not after a state sends a notice
- Ongoing monitoring as thresholds change or new states get added to your footprint
- Marketplace facilitator law guidance, so you know what Amazon and Walmart already collect on your behalf

<!-- block: service-cards | variant: 3-col -->

## Advisory support built around your business, not a billable hour

Most consulting relationships start with a scope of work and end with an invoice that surprises you. Berg Advisors works differently. You pay one flat monthly fee, and that fee covers the phone call, the email, and the fifteen-minute question that saves you a costly mistake three months later.

Our advisory practice runs on a simple idea: businesses that talk to their accountant regularly make better decisions than those that check in once a year at tax time. Whether you're running a multi-channel e-commerce brand, managing a portfolio of rental properties, or overseeing a family office with several entities, you need someone who already understands your numbers when you call.

That's what fixed-fee advisory from a CPA firm with more than 30 years of combined experience looks like in practice.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: advisory-strategy-call.jpg | alt: "Accountant and business owner reviewing cash flow reports on a laptop" | query: "accountant client cash flow meeting" -->
## Strategic planning and cash flow guidance that keeps you ahead

Good decisions come from good information, delivered on a schedule you can plan around. Our core advisory work centers on four things: strategic planning, cash flow management, budget development, and recurring consulting calls that turn financial reporting into an actual conversation.

Strategic planning sessions look at where your business is headed over the next 12 to 24 months, not just the next tax deadline. Cash flow management means you know what's coming in and going out before it becomes a problem, not after. Budget development gives you a working document you'll actually use, reviewed and adjusted as your business changes.

The recurring calls are the part clients tell us matters most. Instead of a one-off project that ends in a binder nobody opens again, you get a standing conversation with your advisory team, quarterly at minimum, where we talk through what changed, what's working, and what needs attention next.

<!-- block: industry-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Advisory tailored to e-commerce, property management, and family offices

Generic consulting advice doesn't hold up against the specific mechanics of your industry. Here's how our advisory work flexes to each niche we serve.

### Multi-channel e-commerce
icon: ChartBar

Selling across Amazon, Shopify, eBay, Etsy, and Walmart means your revenue lives in five different places and your bank account tells only part of the story. We reconcile [multi-channel e-commerce](/industries/e-commerce) platform data into one unified view, so you can see real margin by channel instead of guessing.

### Property management companies
icon: Building2

Tracking income, expenses, and owner distributions across multiple properties and entities in spreadsheets gets unmanageable fast. Advisory work for [property management](/industries/property-management) clients centers on one consolidated view of performance across every property, so distribution and reserve decisions rest on current numbers, not whichever spreadsheet was updated last.

### Family offices
icon: Users

Multiple entities, multiple accounts, and investments that don't report on the same schedule create blind spots. We help [family offices](/industries/family-offices) consolidate that visibility and separate personal from business activity cleanly, so the people managing the money can focus on decisions instead of data-gathering.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: succession-planning-discussion.jpg | alt: "Two business partners discussing long-term planning documents at a desk" | query: "business owners planning discussion office" -->
## Succession planning and long-term business strategy

Not every advisory conversation is about this quarter's cash flow. Business owners who've spent a decade or more building something eventually start asking different questions: What does an exit look like? Who takes over if I step back? What does the business need to be worth, and by when?

Succession planning and risk management are part of our advisory work for exactly that reason. We help you think through ownership transitions, key-person risk, and the financial structure that makes a future sale or transfer smoother, well before you need any of it. These conversations work best started early, alongside the recurring strategic planning calls already built into your engagement, not as a rushed project the year you decide to sell.

<!-- block: feature-grid | variant: 3-col -->

### Flat monthly fees

Want to know who you'd actually be talking to? [Meet the CPAs and EAs](/about-us/meet-the-team) on the advisory team.

Tax season shouldn't be the only time your CPA calls. At Berg Advisors, tax work happens all year: quarterly check-ins, mid-year projections, and plain-English answers to whatever question is keeping you up at night, not just a scramble every March and April.

The firm started in Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, and has grown into a virtual practice serving business owners and individuals in all 50 states, from Delaware County retailers to e-commerce sellers running fulfillment centers in five states. Andrew C. Berg, CPA, built the practice around one idea: a preparer files your return, an advisor helps you keep more of what you earn. Every client gets a fixed monthly fee, a mutual success plan, and a team that already knows the business before a filing deadline lands on the calendar.

<!-- block: service-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Business and personal income tax preparation done right

Filing a return is table stakes. Getting it right, on time, without a surprise invoice afterward, is where a lot of small-business owners get burned by their current preparer.

### Business Tax Preparation
icon: Building2

Federal and state returns for LLCs, S corps, partnerships, and multi-entity structures, prepared by CPAs who already track the books during the year instead of meeting the numbers for the first time each spring.

### Personal Income Tax Preparation
icon: FileText

Individual returns for owners, self-employed professionals, and families with investment income, K-1s, or multi-state filing requirements tied to the business.

### Year-End 1099 Preparation
icon: Receipt

Vendor and contractor 1099 filing handled on schedule, so January doesn't turn into a scramble for missing W-9s and last-minute payment reports.

Every tax engagement runs on a flat monthly fee instead of hourly billing. The cost is set before the work starts, and a phone call or email question won't show up as a surprise line item on next month's invoice. That predictability matters for self-employed professionals and small-business owners who need to budget for accounting costs the same way they budget for rent or payroll.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: quarterly-tax-planning-review.jpg | alt: "Accountant and business owner reviewing quarterly tax planning documents together" | query: "accountant client quarterly review meeting" -->
## Tax planning and strategy that goes beyond filing

Filing a clean return is the finish line. Getting there without an April surprise takes planning that starts in January.

- Quarterly check-ins to review estimated payments, entity elections, and year-to-date profit before liabilities pile up
- Plain-English strategy sessions that translate the tax code into decisions you can actually act on
- Audit protection and IRS representation from Julia Lindner, EA, if a notice ever lands in the mailbox
- Multi-entity and multi-state compliance review from Michael Laudazio, so filings stay accurate as the business grows
- A written mutual success plan that spells out deadlines, deliverables, and who owns each task

Every strategy session gets checked against actual numbers, not last year's assumptions. Business owners who want this built into their monthly accounting can add [advisory and consulting support](/services/advisory) alongside tax planning, so cash flow, budgeting, and tax strategy come from the same team.

<!-- block: industry-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Specialized tax expertise for e-commerce, property management, and family offices

Generic tax software wasn't built for a business selling on four marketplaces, managing thirty rental units, or consolidating three family entities into one return. These are the three niches Berg Advisors built its practice around.

### Multi-Channel E-Commerce
icon: Globe

Sellers running inventory across Amazon, Shopify, eBay, Etsy, and Walmart need accrual-based books that match reality, plus sales tax handling in every state a product ships to. Berg Advisors is one of a small number of full-service U.S. firms built around accrual accounting, inventory costing, and multi-state sales tax nexus for [multi-channel e-commerce sellers](/industries/e-commerce).

### Property Management Companies
icon: Home

Tracking income, expenses, and owner distributions across dozens of properties and entities creates a tax filing headache without centralized books. Entity-level returns, depreciation schedules, and owner K-1s get handled together for [property management companies](/industries/property-management), not as separate projects each spring.

### Family Offices
icon: Users

Consolidated tax visibility across multiple entities, trusts, and investment accounts replaces the spreadsheet-and-guesswork approach many [family offices](/industries/family-offices) inherit from prior advisors. Personal and business filings stay properly separated, coordinated, and on schedule.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: multi-state-sales-tax-map.jpg | alt: "Business owner reviewing a multi-state sales tax map on a laptop" | query: "business owner reviewing map laptop" -->
## Multi-state sales tax nexus guidance for growing businesses

Add a product to a fifth marketplace or open a warehouse in a new state, and nexus rules change with it. A product-based business can trigger sales tax collection obligations in a state it's never set foot in, just by storing inventory there or crossing a revenue threshold.

Andrew C. Berg, CPA, works directly with multi-channel sellers and wholesale distributors expanding into new states, reviewing nexus exposure before it becomes a liability instead of after a state sends a notice. That includes registering in new states, mapping which products are taxable where, and setting a reporting cadence so sales tax doesn't become a year-end scramble.

Most e-commerce-focused accounting shops treat sales tax as a bookkeeping line item. Berg Advisors treats it as a compliance strategy, because a missed nexus threshold in one state can cost more to fix than a full year of accounting fees.

- 30+ years of combined CPA experience across the founding team
- Woodard Top 50 Accounting Firm, named in the 2023 Client Accounting Services Award Spotlight
- Intuit Firm of the Future recognition for building a modern, cloud-based practice

Meet the CPAs, EA, and advisors behind those numbers on the [team page](/about-us/meet-the-team). The relationship is the product here, not just the return.

### Ultimate Consulting Checklists & Tools | Berg Partners

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Practical tools built from real client work

At Berg Advisors, these checklists are not marketing giveaways. They are the same working documents Andrew C. Berg, CPA, and the team use with e-commerce sellers, property management companies, and family offices across the country every month. Thirty years of CPA work taught us that a good checklist catches a bad quarter before it happens, not just a messy folder after the fact.

Each tool below started as an internal process, something built to keep a client's books accurate between calls. We cleaned them up and made them downloadable because the same gaps show up repeatedly: unreconciled marketplace deposits, missing 1099s, owner distributions nobody tracked. Pick the ones that match your business in our [industries](/industries) work and use them as a starting point for a conversation, not a substitute for one.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-right | image: ecommerce-checklist.jpg | alt: "Business owner reviewing multi-channel sales reports on a laptop" | query: "ecommerce seller reviewing sales reports" -->
## Checklists for e-commerce sellers

Multi-channel selling creates a reconciliation problem no spreadsheet fixes by itself. Revenue lands in Amazon, Shopify, eBay, Etsy, and Walmart accounts on different schedules, with different fee structures and different definitions of a completed sale. Our [e-commerce](/industries/e-commerce) checklists walk through the line items most sellers miss.

- Monthly marketplace reconciliation checklist covering Amazon Seller Central, Shopify, and Walmart Marketplace deposit timing
- Inventory accounting checklist for COGS, landed cost, and accrual-basis adjustments
- Multi-state sales tax nexus tracker to flag when a state's economic threshold has been crossed
- Platform fee and chargeback review list for Amazon FBA and Shopify Payments

These come out of work Andrew Berg, CPA, has done building accrual-basis books for growing e-commerce brands, one of the areas where Berg Advisors operates as a full-service U.S. firm.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-left | image: property-management-checklist.jpg | alt: "Property manager reviewing owner distribution statements at a desk" | query: "property manager reviewing financial documents" -->
## Checklists for property management companies

Running books for one property is straightforward. Running them for a dozen properties, three entities, and a handful of owners expecting monthly statements is a different job. Our [property management](/industries/property-management) checklists are organized the way the work actually happens: by entity, then by property, then by owner.

- Monthly owner distribution checklist confirming reserve balances before funds go out
- Multi-property expense categorization guide for shared costs like landscaping, insurance, and management fees
- Entity-by-entity month-end close checklist to keep each LLC's books separate and audit-ready
- Trust account reconciliation checklist for security deposits and prepaid rent

These grew out of ongoing bookkeeping work for property management clients, where one centralized view across every property replaces the spreadsheet juggling most firms leave owners to sort out on their own.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-right | image: family-office-checklist.jpg | alt: "Family office advisor reviewing consolidated investment statements" | query: "financial advisor reviewing investment documents" -->
## Checklists for family offices

Family offices carry a specific kind of complexity: multiple entities, multiple bank accounts, and a real risk of personal and business transactions blending together over time. Our [family office](/industries/family-offices) checklists focus on the two problems that come up most often in these engagements.

- Multi-entity consolidation checklist for combining investment, real estate, and operating entity reporting into one view
- Personal versus business transaction separation guide, built for households managing investment and operating expenses through shared accounts
- Annual entity structure review checklist to confirm each holding is still reporting the way it should

Family offices work with Berg Advisors to get consolidated visibility without hiring a full internal finance team, and these tools reflect what that consolidation actually requires.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image-left | image: tax-close-checklist.jpg | alt: "Accountant organizing tax documents and folders on a desk" | query: "accountant organizing tax documents" -->
## Year-round tax and close checklists for every client

Some checklists apply no matter what industry a business is in. These are the ones sent to nearly every [tax and accounting](/services/tax) client at some point in the year, regardless of whether they sell on Amazon, manage apartment buildings, or run a family office.

- Year-end 1099 preparation checklist covering vendor W-9 collection and filing deadlines
- Monthly close checklist for reconciling bank, credit card, and loan accounts before books are marked final
- Tax document organizer for individuals and businesses preparing for filing season
- New business entity setup checklist for choosing a structure and registering with the right states

Use them on your own, or bring them to a call with a Berg Advisors CPA and work through the gaps together.

A checklist tells you what's missing. A conversation tells you what to do about it. <!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: client-onboarding-documents.jpg | alt: "Business owner signing an engagement letter with a CPA" | query: "business owner signing document office" -->
## New client onboarding documents

What you'll need depends on which service line you're starting with, bookkeeping, tax, or advisory, but a few documents come up for nearly every new engagement:

- Engagement letter outlining scope of work, timeline, and our fixed monthly fee
- New client intake questionnaire covering entity structure, prior-year filings, and accounting software in use
- IRS Power of Attorney (Form 2848) or Tax Information Authorization (Form 8821) if we'll be representing you before the IRS
- Bank, credit card, and platform access authorization so our outsourced accounting team can begin monthly reconciliations

We'll walk through each one with you on your kickoff call rather than emailing a stack of PDFs and disappearing. That's part of the mutual success plan we build for every client at Berg Advisors, not a one-time form drop. Our [outsourced accounting](/services/accounting) and [tax](/services/tax) teams use slightly different intake packets, so let us know which service you're starting with and we'll send the right set.

## Tax preparation forms and checklists

Tax prep at Berg Advisors runs year-round, not just January through April, so several of these documents get used more than once a year:

- Individual tax organizer covering W-2, 1099, K-1, and investment income
- Business tax organizer for S-corps, partnerships, and multi-entity filers
- 1099 filing checklist for contractor and vendor payments due each January
- Document upload checklist listing exactly which statements and prior returns to send before your planning call

Because we handle year-round tax planning and strategy, not just annual filing, several clients use these organizers during quarterly check-ins to project liability before year-end rather than scrambling in March. Michael Laudazio works with multi-entity and multi-state filers on compliance timing, and Julia Lindner, EA, handles document requests tied to IRS notices or audit response. ## Resources for e-commerce, property management, and family office clients

Generic checklists don't work for niche businesses, so we built document sets specific to the industries we know best.

### E-commerce Sellers
icon: Globe

Multi-channel sellers on Amazon, Shopify, eBay, Etsy, and Walmart need a sales tax nexus worksheet to track where they've triggered filing obligations, plus a monthly multi-channel sales report template that reconciles revenue across platforms before it hits your books. ### Property Management Companies
icon: Building2

### Family Offices
icon: Briefcase

Consolidating visibility across entities and investments starts with an entity and investment summary worksheet, along with a personal-versus-business expense separation checklist to keep records clean for every account under the family umbrella. Our [family office](/industries/family-offices) advisory work is built around exactly this kind of consolidation.

Berg Advisors is a virtual firm, so the portal isn't a convenience feature, it's how the relationship works. Clients from coast to coast upload bank statements, tax documents, and entity records through an encrypted portal instead of email attachments, and our team reviews and responds through the same system.

The firm was named a Woodard Top 50 Accounting Firm and recognized as an Intuit Firm of the Future, both tied to how we use technology to keep client communication proactive rather than reactive. If you're a new client, your onboarding email includes a portal invitation with setup instructions. ### Accounting, Bookkeeping, Tax, & Advisory Services
URL: /services

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## One firm for accounting, bookkeeping, tax, and advisory

Most businesses end up juggling three or four separate vendors: a bookkeeper, a tax preparer, a part-time advisor, maybe a payroll service that doesn't talk to any of them. Berg Advisors combines accounting, bookkeeping, tax, and advisory work under one roof, with one team that already knows your numbers before you have to explain them again.

Berg Advisors is a virtual CPA firm rooted in Pennsylvania, serving e-commerce sellers, property management companies, and family offices nationwide. Andrew C. Berg, CPA, has spent more than 30 years building the kind of firm he wanted to hire himself: proactive, plain-spoken, and billed at a flat monthly rate instead of the clock. The three service pillars below, outsourced accounting, tax, and advisory, are built to work together, not as separate line items you have to coordinate yourself.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: bookkeeping-monthly-close-review.jpg | alt: "Accountant reviewing bank reconciliation reports on a laptop screen" | query: "bookkeeper reviewing financial reports laptop" -->
## Outsourced accounting and bookkeeping that keeps your books close-ready

Bookkeeping should do more than produce a report you file away. Our monthly close covers bank and credit card reconciliations, accounts payable and receivable management, and financial reporting built to hold up when a bank, investor, or buyer asks for GAAP-compliant numbers.

For growing businesses moving off cash-basis accounting, that shift matters. Andrew Berg, CPA, works directly with clients converting to accrual accounting ahead of a loan application or an investor round, walking through what changes on the financial statements and why it affects the numbers a lender actually looks at.

Every engagement includes quarterly advisory calls, not just a monthly PDF. We flag the receivable balance creeping up, the margin that slipped a point, or the vendor payment about to land right before a tax deadline, before you have to ask.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: tax-planning-consultation-documents.jpg | alt: "CPA reviewing tax documents and forms with a client at a desk" | query: "tax advisor reviewing documents with client" -->
## Business and personal tax planning and preparation done year-round

Tax season shouldn't be the first time you hear from your CPA. We handle business tax preparation, personal income tax preparation, and year-end 1099 filings, but the bulk of the work happens in the months before any of it is due.

Multi-state sales tax nexus is where this shows up most for product-based businesses. Once you're shipping into a new state, whether from a new warehouse, a third-party logistics provider, or an economic nexus threshold you've crossed, you likely owe sales tax there. Andrew Berg, CPA, advises e-commerce and wholesale clients on registering, filing, and staying compliant as they expand across state lines.

If a notice from the IRS ever does show up, Julia Lindner, EA, represents clients directly in tax resolution and audit matters. Michael Laudazio works with multi-entity and multi-state businesses sorting through overlapping filing requirements, so a return doesn't get filed twice, or missed entirely.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: business-advisory-strategy-meeting.jpg | alt: "Advisor and business owner discussing charts during a strategy meeting" | query: "business advisor strategy meeting charts" -->
## Business advisory and consulting to guide bigger decisions

Clean books answer what happened last month. Advisory work answers what to do next. Our consulting engagements cover strategic planning, cash flow management, budget development, and succession planning, delivered through recurring calls instead of a single annual meeting.

For inventory-heavy businesses outside the pure e-commerce space, think CPG brands, wholesalers, and distributors, Andrew Berg, CPA, provides outsourced CFO services: cash flow forecasting tied to purchase order timing, margin analysis by SKU, and the financial modeling that supports a bank conversation or an equity raise. Veil Velarde, CPA, works with growth-stage businesses that need fractional back-office support without hiring a full finance team.

The point of every advisory call is the same: catch the decision while it's still a decision, not after it's already been made.

## One firm for ecommerce, property management, and family office accounting

Berg Advisors is a CPA firm based in Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, built around three specialties: multi-channel e-commerce, property management, and family offices. The firm works virtually, so a Shopify seller in Ohio and a property manager in Chester County get the same proactive service, the same reporting cadence, and the same team that already understands their industry.

Most CPA firms pick one niche and force every client through the same generic process. Berg Advisors built three distinct service tracks instead, each with its own software stack, reporting rhythm, and specialist attention. Flat monthly fees replace hourly billing across every engagement, so a phone call to ask a question doesn't turn into a surprise line item on next month's invoice.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: ecommerce-multichannel-accounting.jpg | alt: "Ecommerce seller reviewing Amazon and Shopify sales dashboards on a laptop" | query: "ecommerce seller reviewing sales dashboard laptop" -->
## Accounting built for multi-channel ecommerce sellers

Selling on Amazon, Shopify, Etsy, Walmart, and eBay at once means five payout schedules, five fee structures, and five sets of reports that rarely agree with each other. [E-commerce accounting](/industries/e-commerce) at Berg Advisors consolidates that data into one accrual-basis set of books, so gross margin and true profitability show up correctly instead of getting buried in platform fees and reserve holds.

Inventory is where most e-commerce books fall apart. The firm tracks landed costs, COGS by SKU, and inventory in transit, so the balance sheet reflects what a business actually owns rather than what a bank feed assumes.

Multi-state sales tax nexus is the other landmine for growing sellers. Once revenue crosses economic nexus thresholds in a new state, filing obligations follow. Andrew C. Berg, CPA, advises product-based businesses on registering, tracking exposure, and filing correctly through [multi-state sales tax nexus advisory](/services/tax) as they expand into new states, one of the pieces that separates a full-service e-commerce accounting practice from a firm that only reconciles bank feeds.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: property-management-accounting-review.jpg | alt: "Property manager reviewing rental income reports for multiple buildings" | query: "property manager reviewing reports office" -->
## Financial clarity for property management companies in Chester County and nationwide

Property managers juggling a dozen buildings across multiple owner entities know the spreadsheet problem well: one tab per property, formulas that break, and no single number that shows how the portfolio is actually performing. [Property management accounting](/industries/property-management) at Berg Advisors replaces that with one consolidated view of income, expenses, and performance across every property and entity in the portfolio.

Owner distributions get their own tracking, so year-end reconciliation isn't a scramble to figure out who was paid what and when. Trust accounting, CAM reconciliations, and entity-level reporting stay separate on the books but visible from a single dashboard.

Whether a client manages a handful of buildings in Chester County or a multi-state portfolio, the reporting cadence stays the same: monthly close, quarterly strategy calls, and a team already fluent in property management accounting instead of learning it on the client's dime.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: family-office-financial-consolidation.jpg | alt: "Advisor reviewing consolidated investment and entity statements with a family" | query: "financial advisor meeting with family clients" -->
## Discreet, consolidated accounting for family offices

Family offices carry a specific kind of complexity: personal expenses and business entities that have blurred together over years, multiple investment accounts, and a family that wants one clear answer instead of twelve spreadsheets. [Family office services](/industries/family-offices) at Berg Advisors start by untangling that commingling, separating personal transactions from business activity across every entity in the structure.

From there, the firm builds one consolidated view of entities, accounts, and investments, so the family and its outside advisors can see net worth, cash flow, and entity-level performance without requesting five different reports. Access to CPA-level financial expertise means the family isn't staffing an internal accounting department or piecing together information from a bookkeeper who only sees one entity.

The relationship matters as much as the reporting here. Family offices want an advisor who remembers the story behind the structure, not just the numbers inside it. That's the same relationship-first standard Berg Advisors applies to every client.

Hourly billing punishes the exact behavior a good CPA relationship depends on: calling before a decision instead of after. Berg Advisors uses fixed monthly fees for every client, e-commerce, property management, or family office, so questions get asked early and often instead of stacking up until the invoice arrives.

### Accounting, Bookkeeping, & Tax Services for Property Management Companies
URL: /industries/property-management

<!-- block: intro-text | variant: centered -->
## Accounting built around how property management companies operate

Managing properties means managing money in a dozen directions at once: rent rolls, owner draws, security deposit trust accounts, vendor payments, and reserve funds, often spread across several legal entities. Berg Advisors has spent more than 30 years building [outsourced accounting](/services/accounting) systems for landlords, property managers, and real estate holding companies who need that complexity organized, not oversimplified. Woodard named the firm a Top 50 Accounting Firm, and Intuit recognized it as a Firm of the Future, distinctions earned by handling exactly this kind of work.

Berg Advisors operates as a virtual firm, so a property manager in Newtown Square, Pennsylvania works with the same team, the same flat monthly fee, and the same proactive check-ins as one managing units across three states. There's no hourly clock running when you call about a late owner distribution or a new acquisition, and no generic small-business template standing in for actual trust accounting knowledge.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: property-manager-reviewing-statements.jpg | alt: "Property manager reviewing financial statements at a desk with a laptop" | query: "property manager reviewing financial documents" -->
## The bookkeeping challenges unique to multi-unit portfolios

Property management accounting breaks standard small-business bookkeeping in specific ways. Rent collected for one owner's property can't mix with another's. Security deposits need to sit in separate trust accounts under state regulations. Management fees have to be calculated and posted correctly before owner distributions go out. Multiply that across several properties and a handful of LLCs, and one missed reconciliation can throw off owner statements for the entire month.

Most property managers we talk with are still tracking distributions in spreadsheets, reconciling bank feeds by hand, and finding out about a shortfall only after an owner asks why their check is light. Trust accounting adds another layer of risk: getting the separation between client funds and operating funds wrong isn't just messy bookkeeping, it's a compliance problem with a state regulator attached to it. These workflows need to be built around property management mechanics from the start, not retrofitted from a generic chart of accounts.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: consolidated-property-dashboard.jpg | alt: "Laptop screen showing property portfolio financial reports and dashboards" | query: "financial dashboard reports laptop office" -->
## One centralized view of every property, owner, and entity

Instead of piecing together portfolio performance from five different spreadsheets and three bank logins, you get one consolidated system that shows income, expenses, and owner equity across everything you manage. That means fewer late-night reconciliations before an owner call and fewer surprises when a lender or investor asks for financials.

- Property-level and entity-level P&Ls updated on the same schedule every month
- Owner distribution tracking and statements ready before owners start asking
- Trust account reconciliations kept separate, documented, and audit-ready
- Consolidated reporting that rolls up every LLC or holding entity into one view
- A single point of contact who already knows how your portfolio is structured

<!-- block: service-cards | variant: 3-col -->

### Entity-level and portfolio reporting

### Tax preparation and planning

icon: Users

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: cpa-team-meeting-client.jpg | alt: "CPA and client shaking hands after a business meeting in an office" | query: "CPA client meeting handshake office" -->
## Why property managers choose Berg Advisors over hourly-billing generalists

Most general CPA firms treat property management like any other small business and bill hourly for the time it takes to explain trust accounting to them. Berg Advisors built its practice on the opposite premise: more than 30 years of CPA work focused on the industries where standard bookkeeping falls short, including property management, [advisory](/services/advisory) support, and multi-entity reporting.

Every client gets a flat monthly fee agreed on upfront and a mutual success plan built around their portfolio's actual structure. The firm started in Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, and today works with property managers from Chester County to portfolios across the country, all through the same proactive, relationship-driven model. You'll talk to a [team](/about-us/meet-the-team) member who already knows your entity structure, so nobody has to re-explain the setup every March.

If you're closing books at midnight, chasing owner statements, or not entirely sure your trust accounting would survive a state audit, that's worth a conversation. Berg Advisors will walk through your current setup, your entities, and where the gaps are, then show you what a flat monthly fee and a dedicated CPA team would look like for your portfolio.

### Family Office Accounting & Tax Services
URL: /industries/family-offices

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-right | image: family-office-planning-meeting.jpg | alt: "Advisor and family reviewing multi-entity financial statements together" | query: "family financial advisor meeting documents" -->
## Accounting and tax support made for multi-generational wealth

Family offices carry a different kind of complexity than a single business. There's real estate, investment accounts, closely held entities, and often three or more generations with a stake in how it's all managed. Many national firms hand that off to a rotating cast of associates who learn your family's structure once and then move on to the next file.

Berg Advisors has spent more than 30 years working through exactly this kind of complexity, and family offices are one of the core niches we built the practice around, alongside e-commerce and property management. You get a dedicated team that actually knows your entities, your accounts, and your history, backed by flat monthly fees instead of a bill that climbs every time you call with a question. Proactive communication is part of how we operate: expect us to reach out with observations before they turn into problems, not after.

<!-- block: checklist-section | variant: with-image | image: family-office-financial-complexity.jpg | alt: "Stack of financial statements from multiple entities and trusts on a desk" | query: "financial documents multiple entities desk" -->
## Common challenges we solve for family offices

Every family office we work with recognizes at least one of these before we start:

- Consolidated visibility. Money moves across trusts, LLCs, brokerage accounts, and real estate holdings, and by the time someone pulls together a full picture, it's already out of date.
- Commingled finances. Personal and business spending blur together, especially when one family member manages both, and that's exactly where errors and IRS scrutiny tend to start.
- Multi-generational reporting. As wealth passes down, the number of entities and stakeholders grows, and the tracking that worked for one generation stops working for the next.

We've seen these patterns often enough to know they're rarely about a lack of financial sophistication. They're about not having one accounting team responsible for the whole picture, entity by entity, generation by generation.

<!-- block: service-cards | variant: 3-col -->
## Services designed around your family's financial complexity

### Multi-entity bookkeeping and accounting
icon: Building2

We consolidate bookkeeping across every trust, LLC, and holding entity into one reporting structure, so you see the complete financial picture instead of piecing it together from five different sets of books.

### Personal and business tax planning
icon: FileText

Business tax preparation and personal income tax planning happen together, under one roof, so a decision in one area doesn't create a surprise in the other when returns are due.

### Estate and trust accounting
icon: Scale

Trusts and estate structures need accounting that reflects the terms of the documents behind them. We work alongside your estate attorney to keep the numbers consistent with the plan.

### Outsourced CFO advisory
icon: ChartLine

Cash flow across entities, distribution planning, and succession decisions get the same level of strategic attention a full-time CFO would give, minus the full-time salary.

<!-- block: content-split | variant: image-left | image: tax-strategy-planning-session.jpg | alt: "CPA explaining tax strategy documents to a client across a desk" | query: "cpa explaining tax documents client" -->
## Sophisticated tax strategies without the complexity headache

Concentrated wealth raises tax questions a standard 1040 doesn't answer. Which entity should hold a given investment. How distributions from multiple LLCs flow through to a family member's individual return. When it makes sense to restructure ahead of a sale or a generational transfer. These aren't once-a-year questions, and treating them that way is how families end up overpaying.

Andrew Berg, CPA, and the team apply more than 30 years of combined CPA experience to build a year-round plan instead of a once-a-year filing. We translate the strategy into plain language: what it does, why it matters, and what happens if nobody acts before the deadline. No jargon, and no assumption that you should already know how a K-1 flows through to a personal return.

## One team, one plan, total financial clarity

Most families juggling this level of complexity end up with a patchwork: one accountant for the business, another for personal returns, a bookkeeper who doesn't talk to either, and a spreadsheet somewhere trying to hold it all together.

We build a mutual success plan with every family office client, a shared roadmap that spells out what we're tracking, how often we're talking, and what "on track" actually looks like for your entities this year. One team handles the bookkeeping, the tax planning, and the advisory conversations, so nothing falls into the gap between two advisors who've never spoken to each other.

## Resources

### The Monday Five: Five Inventory, COGS and Cash Numbers Every Multi-Channel Seller Should Check Weekly
URL: /resources/the-monday-five-five-inventory-cogs-and-cash-numbers-every-m

Most multi-channel sellers have five tabs open on Monday morning: Seller Central, Shopify, Etsy, eBay, and Walmart Seller Center. Each one shows a sales number. None of them tells you whether you can cover the supplier deposit due in three weeks. That gap is where profitable brands run short on cash, and it is why our CPA team built a short weekly routine we call the Monday Five.

It takes about ten minutes. It uses five numbers, each with a plain-English picture of what good looks like and a trigger for when to pick up the phone. Screenshot it, forward it to another seller, or tape it next to your monitor.

## The Monday Five at a glance

| # | Number | What good looks like | Call us when |
|---|--------|----------------------|--------------|
| 1 | Cash on hand vs. upcoming supplier payments | Cash covers the next 30 days of supplier bills, ads, payroll, and sales tax, with a cushion | Cash drops below 30 days of coverage |
| 2 | Weeks of inventory per top SKU | Weeks on hand exceed your reorder lead time plus 3 to 4 weeks | A top SKU falls inside its lead time |
| 3 | Blended gross margin after fees and returns | Within 2 points of your target, by channel | Blended margin slips more than 3 points |
| 4 | Inventory value tied to the balance sheet | Ledger within 1 to 2 percent of physical counts | Gap exceeds 2 percent |
| 5 | Marketplace payouts still pending | Every channel paid inside its normal window | Any payout is 3+ days late or shrinking |

Here is how to run each one.

## 1. Cash on hand against upcoming supplier payments

Open your bank balances, then list every supplier payment due in the next 30 days. Add ad spend, payroll, credit card payments, and any sales tax remittance. Compare the two totals.

Say you have $86,000 across your accounts. A $40,000 production deposit is due in 10 days and a $35,000 balance lands in 24. That leaves $11,000 for everything else, including a card bill and two weeks of ad spend. The business is healthy and still has a problem.

**What good looks like:** cash covers the next 30 days of known obligations with a cushion, ideally 1.25 times the total. Sellers with long production cycles often want more.

**When to call us:** the moment coverage drops below 30 days. That is the point where a conversation about timing payouts, negotiating terms, or adjusting a purchase order is still cheap. At 5 days, it is a scramble.

## 2. Weeks of inventory on hand for each top SKU

Pick your top five to ten SKUs by revenue. For each one, divide units on hand (including units at Amazon FBA, a 3PL, and in transit) by average weekly units sold across all channels. The answer is weeks of inventory.

This is the weekly cousin of inventory turnover. If a SKU turns 4 times a year, you hold about 13 weeks of stock (52 divided by 4). Looking at it in weeks is more useful on a Monday, because you can hold it up against your lead time.

Example: a top SKU sells 180 units a week across Amazon, Shopify, and Walmart, and you hold 2,700 units. That is 15 weeks. If production takes 6 weeks and shipping another 4, your lead time is 10 weeks. You have a 5-week window before a stockout, which is fine, but not for long.

**What good looks like:** weeks on hand exceed lead time plus a 3 to 4 week buffer. Too much stock is also a flag. A SKU sitting at 40 weeks is cash parked on a shelf.

**When to call us:** when a top SKU falls inside its lead time, or when one sits above 30 weeks. Either one changes your cash picture from Number 1, and we would rather model it with you before you place the order.

## 3. Blended gross margin after fees and returns

This is the number platform dashboards handle worst. Each marketplace reports sales its own way, and none of them includes your landed cost, freight, or the returns that come back a month later.

The fix is gross margin by channel, then a blended number. Revenue minus cost of goods sold, marketplace and payment fees, fulfillment, and returns, divided by revenue. Here is what that looks like for a seller doing $2.4 million a year.

| Channel | Annual revenue | Margin after fees and returns |
|---------|----------------|-------------------------------|
| Amazon | $1,200,000 | 31% |
| Shopify | $700,000 | 44% |
| Walmart | $250,000 | 28% |
| Etsy | $150,000 | 49% |
| eBay | $100,000 | 33% |
| **Blended** | **$2,400,000** | **35.7%** |

Seen this way, Shopify earns more than 13 points of margin over Amazon on the same products. That is the kind of detail that should shape where your next ad dollar goes.

**What good looks like:** blended margin within 2 points of your target, and no channel drifting more than 3 points from its own trailing average. Amazon referral fees alone often run around 15 percent, so small shifts in return rates or fulfillment fees add up quickly.

**When to call us:** if blended margin slips more than 3 points, or one channel goes under your break-even. Usually the cause is a fee change, a landed cost that was never updated, or a return spike. We can usually find it in one conversation if the books are reconciled by channel.

## 4. Inventory value tied to the balance sheet

Your inventory is probably the largest asset on your balance sheet. It is also the line most likely to be wrong when books are kept by cash basis or by platform reports.

Once a week, compare the inventory value in your books against what your warehouse, 3PL, and FBA reports say you hold, priced at landed cost (product, freight, duties, and prep).

Example: your ledger says $412,000 and the counts say $396,000. That is a 3.9 percent gap, or $16,000 of profit you may be overstating. It could be shrinkage, a unit-of-measure mistake, a missing freight invoice, or stock stuck in transit.

**What good looks like:** the ledger within 1 to 2 percent of physical counts. This is also why lenders and investors ask for accrual-basis financials. A balance sheet with a trustworthy inventory line is a balance sheet people will fund. The [IRS Small Business and Self-Employed Tax Center](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed) is a useful reference if you are unsure how your accounting method affects inventory reporting.

**When to call us:** when the gap exceeds 2 percent for two weeks in a row, or whenever a large shipment lands and you are unsure how it was recorded.

## 5. Marketplace payouts still pending

Money that has been earned but not yet deposited is easy to forget. It is also easy to lose track of when five platforms pay on five schedules. Amazon settles on a cycle of roughly two weeks and may hold a reserve. Shopify Payments usually deposits within a few business days. Etsy, eBay, and Walmart each have their own timing.

List what each channel owes you and when it should arrive. If Amazon shows $31,000 unsettled and Walmart $9,000, you know about $40,000 is coming. Add it to the picture from Number 1.

**What good looks like:** every channel paying inside its usual window, with reserves that are stable or shrinking.

**When to call us:** if a payout is three or more days late, a reserve suddenly grows, or the deposit in your bank does not match the settlement report. Those mismatches are exactly what reconciliation is designed to catch, and they get harder to untangle the longer they sit.

## How to run the check in ten minutes

Pick the same time each Monday. Work from a single sheet, or better, a single reporting package, rather than five logins.

1. Check bank balances and list the next 30 days of obligations (3 minutes).
2. Review weeks on hand for your top SKUs (2 minutes).
3. Read blended margin and the by-channel view (2 minutes).
4. Compare inventory value to counts (1 minute).
5. Add up pending payouts (2 minutes).

If you are chasing numbers across platforms and the sheet takes an hour, that is a signal your books are not unified. The Monday Five only works when each number comes from one reconciled source. Otherwise you are comparing a Shopify export to an Amazon report to a bank feed, and none of them agree.

This is why many sellers who outgrow a general-purpose bookkeeper come to us. As a CPA for Shopify and multi-channel sellers, our team has spent 30+ years in accounting and is one of the few full-service U.S. firms specializing in e-commerce accrual accounting, inventory, and multi-state sales tax nexus. We were named a Woodard Top 50 Accounting Firm and an Intuit Firm of the Future. Growth across states also creates sales tax questions, so we watch nexus alongside your margin.

Every client gets a mutual success plan, and the Monday Five fits right into it. We agree on your target margin, your cash floor, and your reorder triggers up front. Then we reach out when a number crosses a line, instead of waiting for you to ask. Fixed monthly fees mean you can call when something looks off without wondering what the call will cost. ## Common Questions

**What are the most useful ecommerce KPIs to track every week?**

Start with cash against upcoming supplier payments, weeks of inventory per top SKU, blended gross margin after fees and returns, inventory value against the balance sheet, and pending marketplace payouts. These five show whether you can pay bills and restock, and they take about ten minutes to review.

**How do I track ecommerce sales across Amazon, Shopify, Etsy, eBay, and Walmart?**

Pull each channel's sales into one set of books on an accrual basis, then reconcile payouts to bank deposits. Platform dashboards report revenue, not profit. A unified ledger lets you see gross margin by channel after fees, returns, and landed cost, which no single marketplace report will show.

**How many weeks of inventory should I keep on hand?**

Hold more than your reorder lead time plus a 3 to 4 week buffer. If production and shipping take 10 weeks, aim for roughly 13 to 14 weeks on your top SKUs. Much beyond 30 weeks usually means cash is tied up in slow stock.

## Talk through your Monday Five with a CPA

If your numbers do not agree across channels, or the weekly check takes longer than ten minutes, it is time for a conversation.
